clue.text: Century old prophecy which helped Britons across the water

definitions.text: which helped Britons across the water

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for century, a hundred
an oracle was a prophecy given by the gods in the ancient world

explanation.surface: An ancient prediction, a hundred years old, that once aided the British in crossing the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: A CORACLE is a small round wicker-and-hide boat used by ancient Britons; the definition is a descriptive phrase rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The early Britons paddled small round hide-covered boats across rivers, so the phrase describes the vessel by its use.

clue.text: The government case

definitions.meaning: the senior ministers who run the country
a cupboard or display case with shelves or drawers

explanation.surface: The state's own legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior ministers form the executive body; the same word names a piece of furniture for storing things.

clue.text: They help to make pretty face in periodical columns

definitions.text: They help to make pretty face
definitions.meaning: evenly proportioned eyes, nose and mouth make an attractive countenance
articles that appear in every issue of a magazine or newspaper

explanation.surface: Beauty tips appearing in magazine columns.
explanation.definitionFit: Symmetrical well-formed facial elements make someone good-looking, and recurring columns in magazines go by the same phrase.

clue.text: Sound sight for instance

definitions.note: the definition stands for the verb meaning to quote as an example

indicators.note: placed before the word, it says we want a word pronounced like the next one

parts.note: the word sight, the faculty of seeing

explanation.surface: Giving a famous view or something audible as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: to quote something 'for instance' is to give it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To quote something as an example or illustration.

clue.text: Jewel of isle!

definitions.meaning: a precious green gemstone
Ireland is poetically called the green island of this name

explanation.surface: Exclaiming about the gem of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Emerald Isle is a poetic name for Ireland, from its green landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a green gemstone, and it completes the poetic nickname for Ireland.

clue.text: So lawful a way to seek custom

parts.note: licit is a formal word for lawful or permitted

explanation.surface: A legitimate method of drumming up business.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit is to ask for trade, as a street vendor or touting salesman does.

clue.text: Bribed squad to go roundabout

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A team paid off so that they travel in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: To square someone is to pay them off or bribe them to cooperate.

clue.text: Let's change just in case

indicators.note: change here means alter the order, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suggestion to switch things over as a precaution.
explanation.definitionFit: Lest is an old-fashioned conjunction meaning for fear that, to avoid the risk of.

clue.text: Party lights on show in Beijing?

definitions.meaning: collapsible paper lamps hung at garden parties
whimsically, any lamps displayed in China's capital

explanation.surface: Festive illuminations displayed in the Chinese capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Folding paper lamps used for festivities are named after China, so any seen in Beijing qualify.

clue.text: Muscular bands with enough fellows to form two quintets

parts.note: a quintet is five, so two of them make ten
dons are fellows or lecturers at a university such as Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Strongmen joined by enough university fellows to form two groups of five musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendons are tough fibrous cords linking muscle to bone.

clue.text: Asks the quiz-master for anether, but misses the point

definitions.meaning: a contestant who pleads for a further item of the quiz is literally pleading for one more query
the idiom describes an argument that evades the real issue by assuming what it should prove

explanation.surface: A quiz contestant keeps pleading for extra items yet fails to grasp what matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, pleading for one more query; idiomatically, an argument that dodges the real issue by assuming its conclusion.

clue.text: Cromwell's head

definitions.meaning: The popular nickname given to Oliver Cromwell
an archaic word for the top of the skull or pate

explanation.surface: The topmost part of Oliver Cromwell's body, perhaps after his exhumation.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Cromwell, Lord Protector of England, was mocked as 'Old Noll'; Noll is a pet form of Oliver.
explanation.definitionFit: Noll was Cromwell's nickname, and in old English usage a noll is the crown of the skull.

clue.text: Esau was dangerous

definitions.meaning: in Genesis Esau is described as covered in thick body growth, unlike his smooth brother Jacob
informally, a risky or frightening situation is called this

explanation.surface: A remark that the biblical Esau was a perilous figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Esau was the shaggy twin of the Bible; in slang a scary, risky situation is described the same way.

clue.text: Planned mode of protest

indicators.note: something planned is arranged anew, so the letters of the next word are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: An organised method of public objection.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is the short informal word for a public demonstration or protest march.

clue.text: Measured up and prepared for paper hanging

definitions.meaning: sorted or assessed according to dimensions
a wall is coated with a gluey wash called size before wallpapering

explanation.surface: Walls that have been measured and readied for decorating.
explanation.definitionFit: Graded by dimensions, or coated with a glue wash that readies walls for wallpaper.

clue.text: Modify a repair

parts.note: to mend is to repair

explanation.surface: An instruction to alter a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to change or correct, as with a law or text.

clue.text: Attempted to engulf Arkansas but lingered

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: tried means attempted
AR is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Arkansas

explanation.surface: Someone tried to swallow up a US state but hung about instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is to linger or stay longer than intended.

clue.text: Piano felts chewed up down under

definitions.meaning: the felt pads that stop a piano string vibrating when a key is released
in Australia, a simple unleavened bread baked in campfire ashes, eaten by bushmen

explanation.surface: Felt parts from a piano being gnawed in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' is Australia; damper is the bushman's bread baked in embers, so it is 'chewed up' there.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano mechanisms use felt-covered pads to mute strings, and Australian campfire bread shares the same name.

clue.text: Excuse the foreword?

definitions.meaning: a false reason given to hide the real one
read whimsically, the material placed before the main body of a book

explanation.surface: Asking whether a book's preface is merely an apology.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretext is a pretended reason; split playfully, it is what comes before the main text of a book.

clue.text: Highly trained soldier gets 100 centavos for giving daytime protection

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, an elite soldier
the Peruvian sol was divided into a hundred centavos

explanation.surface: An elite soldier is paid in Latin American currency for providing protection by day.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunshade carried to protect against the sun's rays during the day.

clue.text: Tied up by trust it could be said

indicators.note: it could be said tells us the answer is pronounced like the word given, not spelt like it

parts.note: the word trust, meaning faith

explanation.surface: Bound and restrained by somebody's faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Trussed means bound tightly, as a chicken is before roasting.

clue.text: Able to bid farewell to religious music

parts.note: to be able is to be capable, as in 'I can'
ta-ta is an informal British goodbye

explanation.surface: Being permitted to say goodbye to church music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ta-ta' is a casual British way of saying goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a choral work, often sacred, such as those Bach wrote for church services.

clue.text: Teased and separated the straw into short lengths

definitions.meaning: mocked in a good-humoured way

definitions.text: separated the straw into short lengths
definitions.meaning: chaff is chopped straw or hay used as animal fodder

explanation.surface: Joshed while cutting straw on the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: To josh someone good-naturedly, and also to cut hay into short pieces for livestock feed.

clue.text: Many set free

indicators.note: free here means released from their fixed order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lots of people released from custody.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a general pardon frees many prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: A general pardon releases large numbers of prisoners at once.

clue.text: Strike breakers that plagued Hamelin

definitions.meaning: an insulting term for workers who refuse to join a strike, like scabs
in the Pied Piper legend the German town was overrun by rodents

explanation.surface: Blacklegs who tormented the town of the Pied Piper.
explanation.definitionFit: Scabs are called by the name of vermin, and the Pied Piper legend tells of the rodents infesting Hamelin.

clue.text: French novelist of the French graduates

parts.note: du is French for 'of the'
MAs are Masters of Arts, holders of a degree

explanation.surface: A writer from France counted among the country's degree-holders.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandre Dumas wrote The Three Musketeers and The Count of Monte Cristo.

clue.text: It teaches only ten letters of the alphabet

annotationWithheld.why: It teaches only ten letters of the alphabet (4): 'It teaches' is the school, but no parse of 'only ten letters of the alphabet' gives the letters without a word doing two jobs, and no source gives the setter's reading
annotationWithheld.clue: It teaches only ten letters of the alphabet

clue.text: Ruin a cosmopolitan party

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is made up of countries from all over the world
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Wrecking an international gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo plans is to wreck or bring them to nothing.

clue.text: Plant producing iron for British fleet

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's navy

explanation.surface: A factory making iron for the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracken and similar leafy green plants that reproduce by spores.

clue.text: Expensive adornments emanating from long lines of subdued aristocracy

parts.note: strings are long lengths of cord or thread
taken as written
P stands for piano, the musical direction to play softly
earls are nobles, members of the aristocracy

explanation.surface: Costly finery that originates from extended families of low-key nobility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subdued' gives P, the musical abbreviation for piano (softly), placed before EARLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Necklaces of threaded pearls are classic luxurious jewellery.

clue.text: Miss a definitive book brought down by the cowboy

parts.note: a miss is a young girl, a lass
the OED, the Oxford English Dictionary, is the definitive reference book of the language

explanation.surface: A girl and an authoritative volume being knocked over by a ranch hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowboys catch and topple cattle by throwing a looped rope over them.

clue.text: Royal family soap opera

definitions.meaning: a line of hereditary rulers, such as the Tudors
an American 1980s prime-time drama about the wealthy Carrington family

explanation.surface: The monarch's household behaving like characters in a TV melodrama.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruling house passing power down generations, and also the title of a glossy 1980s American TV serial.
